newsitem.title: USA: PainWebber raises views on 3 oil companies, cuts 3.
newsitem.headline: PainWebber raises views on 3 oil companies, cuts 3.

text.p: PaineWebber said Friday it had raised its first quarter earnings estimates for Atlantic Richfield Co, Unocal Corp and USX-Marathon Group, and had cut its forecasts for Occidental Petroleum Corp, Phillips Petroleum Co and Exxon Corp.

It also forecast rising prices for the benchmark West Texas Intermediate crude throughout the year, widening U.S. refining margins, and rising natural gas wellhead prices after a dip in the second quarter.
"On average, we expect first quarter 1997 earnings for the major oils to be 12 percent above last year's first quarter results," said PaineWebber analyst Steven Pfeifer.
The estimate on ARCO was raised to $2.70 a share from $2.55, Unocal to $0.73 from $0.68, and Marathon to $0.55 from $0.50.
Phillips was cut to $0.94 a share from $1.04, Occidental to $0.43 from $0.52, and Exxon to $1.63 from $1.73.
The upgrades are due to increased expectations for oil and gas earnings and, in the case of Marathon, increased expectations for refining and marketing, Pfeifer said.

The downgrades are due to lower than expected chemical earnings for Occidental, lower gas processing and liquids income for Phillips, and lower expectations for refining and marketing and oil and gas income for Exxon, he said.

PaineWebber is forecasting an average price per barrel of $23.05 for West Texas Intermediate crude for the first quarter, $20.50 for the second quarter, $21.00 for the third quarter, and $21.50 for the fourth quarter.

It sees natural gas wellhead prices declining to $1.85 per thousand cubic feet in the second quarter from $2.52 in the first quarter, followed by rises to $1.97 in the third quarter and $2.22 in the fourth quarter.
U.S. Refining margins are expected to widen to $3.53 per barrel in the first quarter from $2.89 in the 1996 fourth quarter and $2.77 for the whole of 1996.
